hazards.control: Only qualified people at the drive, transformer, and junction box; lockout before cable work.
Bleed the tubing and casing to zero and verify before breaking any connection.

name: Electric submersible pump system
function: A multistage centrifugal pump driven by a downhole electric motor on the tubing tail, powered through a cable from a drive at surface: the high-rate lift method.

tabs.overview: Bottom to top: the motor (three-phase induction), the seal or protector section that isolates motor oil from well fluid and takes the thrust, the intake or gas separator, the multistage pump, and the discharge into the tubing. A flat cable runs up the tubing under clamps to a wellhead penetrator, then to a junction box, the variable speed drive, and a transformer at surface. Rates from a few hundred to more than a hundred thousand barrels per day; the simulator draws the drive and transformer skid, the junction box, and the cable at the tree, and the motor, seal, intake, and pump on the tubing downhole.
tabs.engineering: Needs casing larger than about 4-1/2 in.; efficiency drops below a few hundred barrels per day; sensitive to sand and free gas; sized from the inflow and the tubing head pressure; run per API RP 11S.
tabs.connections: Tubing (UC); cable and penetrator at the tubing hanger; power from the pad or the grid.
tabs.safety: Medium-voltage cable and drive; lockout before any cable, penetrator, or drive work.
tabs.evidence: PetroWiki sucker-rod lift, ESP, and gas lift pages (S39, S40, S41); API 11AX, 11E, 11S, 11V (S43 to S46); field practice (S9). Generic geometry; not an OEM design.
tabs.operations: Run with the tubing on a rig; started and ramped on the drive; watched on downhole sensor data.
tabs.failure_modes: Motor burn from overheating or low flow, cable damage during running, gas lock, sand wear of stages, seal failure.
